title: Four Cross-Checks
subtitle: The first step is to reduce it to a quartic equation without a cubic term. The second step ... Ugh, #$%@ this math!

trails.title: Decryption Team Personnel List
trails.description: Puzzles and solvers, now, they're all here.

content.text:
※ Ulrich—Approved

Reasons for selection: The most skilled cryptologist in Laplace, also the most brilliant expert in arcane cryptography. In addition, his energy consumption ratio is excellent, capable of high quality work for 72 hours with only two supplies needed. Recommended for selection as the leader of the decryption team.

Team leader's comments: This assessment of mine is incorrect; this record has since been updated to 360 hours. Nevertheless, I agreed. 

※ Dawkins—Approved

Reasons for selection: Dawkins is an expert in linguistics. We need more of such people when the origin of incantations is unknown.

Team leader's comments: Dawkins is talented but lacks a sense of seriousness, as evidenced by his inappropriate jokes. Do not let him work alone—assign a serious staff member to supervise him, and also use a cold humor punishment device, setting the penalty at 3 pounds a joke.

※ Richard—Approved

Reasons for selection: Richard is an excellent theoretical mathematician and is able to provide us with advice from a mathematical perspective.

Team leader's comments: Richard is only cautious when solving math problems, but averages three collisions with table corners per day. He also needs a supervisor to prevent such accidents during experiments.

※ Matthew—Approved

Reasons for selection: Matthew has excellent decision-making skills. His fighting spirit will surely bring about important breakthroughs in our decryption work.

Team leader's comments: He's just too impulsive. I do not recommend letting him make any decisions, otherwise an explosion in the lab will be the least of our worries.

※ Williams—Approved

Reasons for selection: Williams has a meticulous thought process. He excels at finding loopholes that others cannot—perhaps he can assist Matthew and prevent him from making any egregious mistakes.

Team leader's comments: Williams is what we call an introvert. His penchant for discovery doesn't mean he'll be good at communicating his findings. He should be left alone to deal with verification.

※ Victor—Approved

Reasons for selection: Victor has a leapfrogging thinking pattern and can keep research from getting stuck.

Team leader's comments: Victor is good, sure, it's just that his ideas are sometimes incomprehensible. Do NOT let him team up with Dawkins—he will definitely end up paying 3 pounds for Dawkins to tell a joke. I can assure you, putting a weirdo and a dark humor fanatic together will cause us problems.

※ Adler—Pending

Reasons for selection: Adler's recommendation is not only because he is an excellent cryptologist, but also because this decryption is not just a task for arcanists—we need opinions from humans as well.

Team leader's comments: I have my reservations. It's not that the team doesn't need humans, but it shouldn't be a silent enigma who hasn't been seen in public for eight years.

items.text: Four Cross-Checks

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: Damn! You narcissistic, fat-headed, humanocentrist freaks!

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: You are the crazy ones! And I, I will prove myself right!

items.speaker: Researcher II
items.text: Seriously!? Can someone please bring Matthew back to the rehab center? That mask has made him crazy!
The researcher's arms flail wildly as he stumbles across the shiny silver floor, adding more to the chaos.
Amidst the mayhem, a bottle of alcohol on the ground bursts into bright blue flames.
And then, two metal feet stomp across the fire without hesitation.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Any progress?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Not much. We've called all the experts here, but so far it's been a waste of time. Not even a bodily reaction when reciting the text.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: It doesn't belong to any known language, nor follow any linguistic rules.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Many are starting to doubt the accuracy of the incantation. After all, it was copied down by a novice investigator with her arcane skill, not her supervisor.
The door is pushed open.
The spacious room is now packed with people.
They're all gathered around a radio on the table.

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: Ms. Marcus, can you confirm that the incantation you dictated was correct?

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: We also learned that you witnessed a visual recording of Arcana performing her arcane skill, depicted through images recreated by a pure-blooded arcanist. Is that right?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes, to be precise, I saw it in the memories of Isolde, a former member of Manus Vindictae, using Ms. Kakania's arcane mirror.

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: Can you attest to the accuracy of this memory?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I can't say.

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: Do you deem the reflection of Ms. Kakania's arcane mirror to be accurate, factual, and without misinterpretation?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I'm not sure.

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: Can you confirm that your arcane skill, "Read," was performed correctly, and provided an unbiased, objective, and flawless interpretation?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I, I don't know about that either.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But I saw it with my own eyes. I heard the chanting.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I don't know what language that was, but that's how I heard it, and I've written it down phonetically!

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: Please calm down. We are only verifying the details.

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: The Foundation has dispatched a special operations squad to you in Vienna. Please make sure the two other arcanists involved will return to the Foundation with you.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I ... Understood.
The call ends. The liaison removes the headset.
The result is far from ideal. Her face is pale, as lifeless as her mechanical colleagues.
This? Is this it?
A sarcastic voice cuts through the air as a man pushes through to the front.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: "An ancient miracle, a circle of salvation!"

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: /eɪ u:.nə 'sa.kəʊ/ ... a Tuna Psycho?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: An inexplicable incantation transcribed by an arcanist based on what she saw in the memory of another arcanist recreated by yet another arcanist.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That's as convoluted as a dream within a dream within a dream. To think they wanted an "objective restoration."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I mean, if Gnosis is so reliable and can really cross-check not only once, but FOUR times, it should have long replaced science by now.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: With this level of uncertainty, we might have better luck asking typewriter monkeys to randomly give us the answer to the "Storm" immunity!

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Adler?! Why are you here?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I requested his participation on the cryptography team.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: He is a human, but he excels in the field of cryptography.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: But ...
The man takes a grim step forward.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And why can't I be here?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Is it because Greta Hofmann's my sister?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And this—is this what a respectable and honorable member of the Foundation gave her life to retrieve? Is this the ritual she died for?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Oh, riiight. It wasn't even her who retrieved the ritual. It was her student.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You are not currently on the official roster. You can leave at any time.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Leave? Why should I leave?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I have every right to know what my sister died for!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Well, now. Get to work, people. Let's decipher this great mystery and see what it'll bring us.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Salvation, or oblivion?
He leaves sneering, waving the note with the phonetic spelling in his hand.
The farce is finally over. The room is at peace again.
The cryptography team turns to the robot, awaiting her instructions.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Return to your stations, please.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Let us not dismiss its credibility until we have exhausted every possibility.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Also ...
She calmly turns her head.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Add Adler Hofmann into the cryptography team roster.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: The cryptography lead hesitates for a moment, surprised. Nevertheless, he nods and quickly leaves the room.
The phone on the wall, used for internal communication, begins to ring.

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: "Storm" Observation and Research Center.

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: Noted. I will make sure Ms. Lucy is aware of that.
The liaison puts down the phone and turns to the robot, a flicker of panic on her face.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What is the matter?

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: It's a call from the rehab center, about the previous study on the Manus mask.

items.speaker: Liaison Staff I
items.text: Ma'am, I think you should go see this in person.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Very good, Matthew. Now tell us, what did you hear?
The already narrow corridor is now filled with security guards.
The room they're guarding is heavily secured, isolated behind three layers of tempered glass.
A patient sits in the room with a mask on his face.

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: Voices, those voices! The inaudible murmurs, the frightening whispers, they worm into my ears!

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: I told you before. I wrote about this before! But you dismissed them as manic episodes. Haha, hahahaha!

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Did you put on the mask?

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: Yes. How else would I know that I was right?

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: And now I know! And never have I heard them so clearly. They are screaming inside my head!

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: Their temptations, their promises! I just have to let go of my brain. Can you hear it? The benevolent Mother is speaking!
His nails dig deep into his palms, as if fighting an overwhelming impulse.

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: Now, I can write the ultimate paper!

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Who is this "Mother"?
She is answered by a loud crash. The researcher throws himself against the glass, gasping in horror and scratching helplessly at the surface.

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: No, I can't say any more! They see me. They've come for me.

items.speaker: Researcher I
items.text: Kill me! Kill me now!
It is too late to beg for mercy. His scream is abruptly silenced as his head explodes open behind the glass barrier.
Amidst the splatter of blood and brain, a new being emerges from the remnants of his flesh.

items.speaker: Manus Follower
items.text: *roar*
The alarm blares loudly.
A Manus follower wriggles up from the bloody floor, holding a triangle in hand. He lets out a loud cry, reminiscent of a newborn's first wail.
The liaison ends the call, cutting off the horrid sounds on the other end of the phone.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Suspend all research on the Manus mask at once. Its dangers far outweigh the potential benefits.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Seal away all equipment and share only a controlled account of the incident with others. We cannot afford to have another researcher try on the mask again.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Now. Clean this up.

items.speaker: Laplace Safety Officer
items.text: Yes, ma'am.
The airlock door hisses open, a squad of armed guards storms into the room under the cover of sleeping gas.
On the other side of the glass, the robot turns away from the scene, categorizing yet another set of "Storm" research data as irrelevant and filing it away as waste in her memory.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Another dead end.
TO BE CONTINUED…
